items.title: Madras High Court dismisses election petition against Colachel MLA Tharahai Cuthbert
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently dismissed a petition challenging the election of Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) Tharahai Cuthbert from the Colachel constituency of Tamil Nadu's Kanyakumari district [ SM Anthony Muthu v. Tharahai Cuthbert ]. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy was dealing with an election petition filed by a rival candidate who believed he should have received more votes because of his work in the constituency. The Court observed that it is ultimately the electorate that decides whom to vote for. The mere belief that a candidate's public service should have fetched him more votes cannot be a ground to doubt the counting process, it said. " It may be true that he has done good work. But on the polling day, it is the electorate that decides whom to vote for. In a democracy, every person who does good public service can expect people to vote for him . But to impugn the count, this belief alone is not enough. " Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy Madras High Court It is the electorate that decides whom to vote for. items.title: A day inside a Delhi SIR camp: Forms, confusion and long days
items.summary: Delhi is currently undergoing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, with the Election Commission extending the deadline to submit forms to August 17. Booth Level Officers are handling everything from distributing and collecting forms to digitising the data. To make the process easier, some local residents have set up small camps in their homes to help people fill out and submit their forms. We visited one such camp, where voters faced several challenges in understanding and completing the process. For many, SIR has emerged as a confusing exercise. Some also expressed fears that they could lose their citizenship because of the process. The term ‘relative’ used in the form has added to the confusion, with voters, volunteers, and even some polling officials unsure about how it should be interpreted. Abida, who is unhappy with the government and no longer votes, came to the camp after people told her that failing to fill out the form could get her expelled from Delhi. “Even if I fill out the form, will you stop the demolition?” she asked us. items.title: Advocates acting as insolvency professionals liable to collect, deposit GST: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. items.title: Arbitrating a class action?
items.summary: On June 8, 2026, the Supreme Court closed the doors on India's most significant shareholder class action in 3 paragraphs of consent. The Jindal Poly Films Ltd v. Monet Securities Pvt Ltd was not an in personam dispute but an in rem dispute. items.title: Tamil Nadu: Nine-year-old girl allegedly sexually assaulted while walking home
items.summary: A nine-year-old Class 4 student was allegedly sexually assaulted by an unidentified man while she was walking home in Denkanikottai in Tamil Nadu’s Krishnagiri district on the evening of August 12, Wednesday. The child was walking home with three other children, but the three reached their homes before her, leaving her alone when the alleged assault took place, according to police. The incident was reported around 1 am on Thursday after the child’s mother lodged a complaint with the Denkanikottai All Women Police Station (AWPS). Police have registered an FIR under Section 87 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) (kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc) and Section 5(6) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The child was taken to Krishnagiri Government Hospital for a medical examination. Police said the examination will help determine whether a sexual assault took place. A police team has also visited the scene and is collecting evidence and other information as part of the investigation. The child does not know the identity of the alleged accused, but has told police that she would be able to identify him.

items.title: Nearly a century ago, Dravidian magazines were advocating for women’s reproductive freedom
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The debate over abortion in Tamil Nadu has acquired a new political and religious context after Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar participated in the fifth National March for Life in Chennai on August 8 and 9 and spoke against abortion. He said at the event that life begins at conception and said the issue would be brought to the attention of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. India’s abortion law wasn’t always about a woman’s right to choose. Under the colonial-era IPC, abortion was largely a criminal offence, but the unsafe abortions and deaths that followed led the government-appointed Shantilal Shah Committee to recommend changes. Its recommendations eventually led to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act in 1971, allowing abortion in specified circumstances. But nearly a century ago, the question of controlling pregnancy was being debated in the pages of Kudi Arasu and Pagutharivu , magazines associated with the Self-Respect Movement and founded by Dravidian icon Periyar.
